newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Foreigners impatient with Portugal bond futures.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners impatient with Portugal bond futures.

text.p: Foreign investors are growing impatient with the slow implementation of a repo market and other changes seen as vital to give volume to Portugal's anaemic bond futures contract, analysts said on Thursday.

The continuing lack of the repo contract, the pending regulations on the taxing of investment funds and the continuing exclusion of pension funds and insurers have left market-markers with a difficult job of providing liquidity.
"It is unfortunate the length of time it takes for things to happen in Portugal," said one London trader with a large investment bank.
"Final investors are out of the market because the conditions are not right, principally from the fiscal point of view," said Miguel Pessanha of Banco Portugues do Atlantico.
"The foreigners cannot enter (the market) because they don't have the means (the repo) to finance themselves," he said.

Since the futures started trading on June 20, just 116,000 contracts have traded in the 10-year interest rate contract. This is equal to only two day's business in Spain's futures market in Barcelona.

According to a source close to Portugal's Financial Markets Committee (CMVM), the market watchdog, the CMVM will soon present the final blueprint for the long-awaited repo market to the Finance Ministry.
The plan was drawn up with the Bank of Portugal and the Oporto Futures Exchange, where the repo market will be based.
CMVM has already given the green light for investment funds to operate on the futures market, but pension and insurance funds are awaiting approval from the Insurance Institute of Portugal.
Traders said the Portuguese bond market already operates in the shadow of Spain, but the lack of adequate instruments, such as the repo, was only pushing it further into the background.
"The (10-year) future contract is similar to Spain and a lot less liquid," said the trader at the London investment bank.

"The repos are essential to encourage the international market-markers. The international investment banks cannot operate (at the moment) in a cheap and efficient way," said Manuel Girao, in charge of Portuguese capital markets and derivatives for Credit Swisse Financial Products (CSFP).

The average cost of entering and exiting (the spread using the bid/ask prices of) the Portuguese 10-year bond futures an jump to 13,000 escudos from 7,000 escudos in moving from 20 to 160 contracts, traders said.
"In effect, these 13,000 escudos are what the investor needs to see the contracts gain before he starts to earn any money, and it is a lot," said one analyst.
